lede: Mountain Village Council meets Thursday with something worth tracking: a resolution to set a sale price appreciation cap on deed-restricted units — the fine print that determines whether affordable housing actually stays affordable or quietly drifts out of reach. Telluride's Planning and Zoning Commission also meets Thursday, with a public hearing on the school district's employee housing proposal for the middle-high school site at 725 W Colorado. On the lighter side, the week is stacked with live music, the Telluride Mountain Run, and farmers markets on both ends of the valley.

notable.stake: Appreciation cap vote decides if deed-restricted units stay truly affordable long-term.
